requirements.text: The system shall provide a graphical user interface to all functions of the system.
Grid technologies shall be utilized to provide secure and reliable communications to remote computing resources.
The web portal components shall integrate into the Dataportal Web Server at NCAR
The compute node software shall be developed and deployed for the Hemisphere Linux cluster at CU
The system shall provide a web based (portal) user interface for all aspects of the system.
The system shall use the Globus toolkit.
The system will use the NCAR Mass Storage System for all file based storage.
All GridBGC users shall be required to have valid NCAR Gatekeeper accounts to use the system.
The system shall retrieve all user information from the Gatekeeper account system.
The system shall support the following user roles: User and Administrator.
The system shall provide a means to request that the user account be deleted from the system.
The system shall require the user to enter their username and password to login to the system.
The system shall allow portal administrators the ability to control template submissions rights.
The system shall prevent the user from changing object/project values once that project has been used in a model run.
The system shall support 3 types of objects: List, Grid, and Parameterization.
The system shall require the users enable cookies to use the system.
The system shall allow users the ability to store data on the NCAR Mass Storage System.
The system shall use TLS 1.2 or higher for all web portal traffic and GSI-authenticated secure channels for all grid-based communications.
The system shall implement secure session management with a maximum idle timeout of 30 minutes and regenerate session identifiers upon login.
All data in transit between the web portal, compute nodes, and the NCAR Mass Storage System shall be encrypted using industry-standard protocols (e.g., HTTPS/TLS, GSI-SSH).
The system shall maintain an immutable audit log of all administrative actions, including account approvals, role assignments, and job terminations, for a minimum of 1 year.
All sensitive user data and credentials stored on the NCAR Mass Storage System shall be encrypted at rest using AES-256 or equivalent.
The system shall maintain a 99.9% uptime for communication channels between the portal and compute nodes, with automatic retry logic for transient network failures.
The system shall implement checkpointing for all model runs to allow resumption from the last successful state in the event of a compute node failure.
The system shall perform automated daily integrity checks on all file references in the NCAR Mass Storage System and flag orphaned or corrupted files for administrative review.
The system shall process and return status updates for model runs within 5 seconds of a user request, and support concurrent execution of at least 50 simulation jobs.
Define specific latency targets for UI responsiveness and throughput/completion time targets for Daymet and BiomeBGC modeling runs.
Specify the expected concurrent user load and the projected data storage growth rate to ensure the architecture can scale.
Define acceptable I/O latency thresholds for reading/writing datasets from the MSS to ensure model run times are not bottlenecked by storage access.
Define the maximum supported simulation scale (e.g., maximum number of sites or PFTs per run) to prevent system exhaustion.
